title: OSHA construction Introduction to OSHA study guide
description: Introduction to OSHA study guide: the OSHA poster, inspections, complaints, citations, contests, injury records and severe injury reporting (29 CFR 1903, 1904).
intro: This guide covers two OSHA rules that apply to construction employers as they do to other employers: 29 CFR Part 1903 (inspections, complaints, citations and contests) and 29 CFR Part 1904 (recording and reporting work-related injuries and illnesses). It sets out what the rule text states on the OSHA poster, how inspections and the walkaround work, employee complaints, imminent danger, citations and their posting, contests and abatement, who must keep injury records, the 300, 300-A and 301 forms, and reporting fatalities and severe injuries. Penalty dollar amounts are left out because they change every year. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

topics.name: The OSH Act and the OSHA poster

points.text: Part 1903 explains that the OSH Act requires every covered employer to provide employment and a place of employment free from recognized hazards that are causing or are likely to cause death or serious physical harm to employees.
points.quote: requires, in part, that every employer covered under the Act furnish to his employees employment and a place of employment which are free from recognized hazards that are causing or are likely to cause death or serious physical harm to his employees.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.1, Purpose and scope (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Each employer must post and keep posted the notice (poster) furnished by OSHA that informs employees of their protections and obligations under the Act.
points.quote: Each employer shall post and keep posted a notice or notices, to be furnished by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, U.S. Department of Labor, informing employees of the protections and obligations provided for in the Act

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.2, Posting of notice; availability of the Act, regulations and applicable standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The notice goes in a conspicuous place where notices to employees are customarily posted, and the employer must make sure it is not altered, defaced or covered by other material.
points.quote: Such notice or notices shall be posted by the employer in each establishment in a conspicuous place or places where notices to employees are customarily posted. Each employer shall take steps to insure that such notices are not altered, defaced, or covered by other material.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.2, Posting of notice; availability of the Act, regulations and applicable standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: For physically dispersed activities such as construction, the notice must be posted at the location to which employees report each day.
points.quote: Where employers are engaged in activities which are physically dispersed, such as agriculture, construction, transportation, communications, and electric, gas and sanitary services, the notice or notices required by this section shall be posted at the location to which employees report each day.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.2, Posting of notice; availability of the Act, regulations and applicable standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: If the employer has obtained copies of the Act, the regulations and the applicable standards, it must make them available on request to any employee or the employee's authorized representative, on the same day or at the earliest mutually convenient time.
points.quote: If an employer has obtained copies of these materials, he shall make them available upon request to any employee or his authorized representative for review in the establishment where the employee is employed on the same day the request is made or at the earliest time mutually convenient to the employee or his authorized representative and the employer.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.2, Posting of notice; availability of the Act, regulations and applicable standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Compliance Safety and Health Officers (CSHOs) are authorized to enter without delay and at reasonable times any workplace where an employee of an employer works, including a construction site.
points.quote: Compliance Safety and Health Officers of the Department of Labor are authorized to enter without delay and at reasonable times any factory, plant, establishment, construction site, or other area, workplace or environment where work is performed by an employee of an employer

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.3, Authority for inspection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: If entry or an employee representative's accompaniment is refused, the CSHO must end the inspection or limit it to areas with no objection, find out why, and immediately report the refusal to the Area Director, who consults the Regional Solicitor about action that can include compulsory process (such as an inspection warrant).
points.quote: the Safety and Health Officer shall terminate the inspection or confine the inspection to other areas, conditions, structures, machines, apparatus, devices, equipment, materials, records, or interviews concerning which no objection is raised.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.4, Objection to inspection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Advance notice of inspections may not be given except in the listed situations, such as apparent imminent danger, so the employer can abate the danger as quickly as possible.
points.quote: Advance notice of inspections may not be given, except in the following situations: (1) In cases of apparent imminent danger, to enable the employer to abate the danger as quickly as possible;

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.6, Advance notice of inspections (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: When advance notice is allowed, it may not be given more than 24 hours before the inspection, except in apparent imminent danger situations and other unusual circumstances.
points.quote: Advance notice in any of the situations described in paragraph (a) of this section shall not be given more than 24 hours before the inspection is scheduled to be conducted, except in apparent imminent danger situations and in other unusual circumstances.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.6, Advance notice of inspections (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: At the end of the inspection, the CSHO confers with the employer and informally advises it of any apparent violations, and the employer may bring pertinent information to the CSHO's attention.
points.quote: At the conclusion of an inspection, the Compliance Safety and Health Officer shall confer with the employer or his representative and informally advise him of any apparent safety or health violations disclosed by the inspection.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.7, Conduct of inspections (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: A representative of the employer and a representative authorized by the employees must be given an opportunity to accompany the CSHO during the physical inspection, to aid the inspection.
points.quote: A representative of the employer and a representative authorized by his employees shall be given an opportunity to accompany the Compliance Safety and Health Officer during the physical inspection of any workplace for the purpose of aiding such inspection.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.8, Representatives of employers and employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: During an inspection, any employee must be given an opportunity to bring any violation he or she believes exists to the CSHO's attention.
points.quote: During the course of an inspection, any employee shall be afforded an opportunity to bring any violation of the Act which he has reason to believe exists in the workplace to the attention of the Compliance Safety and Health Officer.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.10, Consultation with employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: An employee or employee representative who believes a violation exists in the workplace where the employee works may request an inspection by notifying the Area Director or a CSHO.
points.quote: Any employee or representative of employees who believe that a violation of the Act exists in any workplace where such employee is employed may request an inspection of such workplace by giving notice of the alleged violation to the Area Director or to a Compliance Safety and Health Officer.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The complaint must be put in writing, state the grounds with reasonable particularity, and be signed by the employee or representative.
points.quote: Any such notice shall be reduced to writing, shall set forth with reasonable particularity the grounds for the notice, and shall be signed by the employee or representative of employees.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The employer gets a copy of the complaint, but if the person who filed it asks, his or her name and the names of employees mentioned in it must not appear on that copy or on any record the Department of Labor releases.
points.quote: upon the request of the person giving such notice, his name and the names of individual employees referred to therein shall not appear in such copy or on any record published, released, or made available by the Department of Labor.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: If the complaint meets the requirements and there are reasonable grounds to believe the violation exists, the Area Director must have an inspection made as soon as practicable. The inspection is not limited to the matters in the complaint.
points.quote: Inspections under this section shall not be limited to matters referred to in the complaint.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Section 11(c)(1) of the Act, quoted in 1903.11, prohibits discharging or discriminating against an employee for filing a complaint, testifying, or exercising any right under the Act.
points.quote: No person shall discharge or in any manner discriminate against any employee because such employee has filed any complaint or instituted or caused to be instituted any proceeding under or related to this Act

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: When a CSHO concludes that conditions could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm immediately or before the danger can be removed through normal enforcement, the CSHO must inform affected employees and employers and say a civil action to restrain the conditions is being recommended.
points.quote: he shall inform the affected employees and employers of the danger and that he is recommending a civil action to restrain such conditions or practices and for other appropriate relief in accordance with the provisions of section 13(a) of the Act.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.13, Imminent danger (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Citations and proposed penalties may still be issued for an imminent danger even if the employer immediately eliminates the imminence of the danger after being told.
points.quote: Appropriate citations and notices of proposed penalties may be issued with respect to an imminent danger even though, after being informed of such danger by the Compliance Safety and Health Officer, the employer immediately eliminates the imminence of the danger and initiates steps to abate such danger.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.13, Imminent danger (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.name: Citations, contests and abatement

points.text: After reviewing the inspection report, the Area Director issues either a citation or a notice of de minimis violations (violations with no direct or immediate relationship to safety or health). It is issued even if the employer immediately abates the violation.
points.quote: An appropriate citation or notice of de minimis violations shall be issued even though after being informed of an alleged violation by the Compliance Safety and Health Officer, the employer immediately abates, or initiates steps to abate, such alleged violation.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.14, Citations; notices of de minimis violations; policy regarding employee rescue activities (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: No citation may be issued after 6 months following the occurrence of the alleged violation.
points.quote: No citation may be issued under this section after the expiration of 6 months following the occurrence of any alleged violation.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.14, Citations; notices of de minimis violations; policy regarding employee rescue activities (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: In setting a proposed penalty, the Area Director considers the size of the business, the gravity of the violation, the employer's good faith, and the history of previous violations. No penalties are proposed for de minimis violations.
points.quote: giving due consideration to the appropriateness of the penalty with respect to the size of the business of the employer being charged, the gravity of the violation, the good faith of the employer, and the history of previous violations

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.15, Proposed penalties (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: On receiving a citation, the employer must immediately post it (or a copy), unedited, at or near each place an alleged violation occurred. Notices of de minimis violations need not be posted.
points.quote: Upon receipt of any citation under the Act, the employer shall immediately post such citation, or a copy thereof, unedited, at or near each place an alleged violation referred to in the citation occurred, except as provided below.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.16, Posting of citations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The citation must stay posted until the violation is abated or for 3 working days, whichever is later. Filing a notice of contest does not end this duty unless the Review Commission issues a final order vacating the citation.
points.quote: Each citation, or a copy thereof, shall remain posted until the violation has been abated, or for 3 working days, whichever is later.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.16, Posting of citations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: An employer that wants to contest a citation or proposed penalty must notify the Area Director in writing, postmarked within 15 working days of receiving the notice of proposed penalty, and say whether it contests the citation, the penalty, or both.
points.quote: Such notice of intention to contest shall be postmarked within 15 working days of the receipt by the employer of the notice of proposed penalty. Every notice of intention to contest shall specify whether it is directed to the citation or to the proposed penalty, or both.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.17, Employer and employee contests before the Review Commission (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: An employee or employee representative may file a written notice alleging that the abatement period fixed in the citation is unreasonable, postmarked within 15 working days of the employer's receipt of the notice of proposed penalty or notice that no penalty is proposed.
points.quote: file a written notice with the Area Director alleging that the period of time fixed in the citation for the abatement of the violation is unreasonable.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.17, Employer and employee contests before the Review Commission (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Working days are Monday through Friday, not counting Saturdays, Sundays or Federal holidays. In counting 15 working days, the day the notice is received is not counted and the last day is.
points.quote: Working days means Mondays through Fridays but shall not include Saturdays, Sundays, or Federal holidays. In computing 15 working days, the day of receipt of any notice shall not be included, and the last day of the 15 working days shall be included.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.22, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: An affected employer, employee or employee representative may request an informal conference with the Assistant Regional Director. A conference or request does not stop the 15-working-day period for filing a notice of contest.
points.quote: No such conference or request for such conference shall operate as a stay of any 15-working-day period for filing a notice of intention to contest as prescribed in § 1903.17.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.20, Informal conferences (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Within 10 calendar days after the abatement date, the employer must certify to OSHA that each cited violation has been abated, unless the CSHO saw the abatement within 24 hours during the on-site inspection and noted it in the citation.
points.quote: Within 10 calendar days after the abatement date, the employer must certify to OSHA (the Agency) that each cited violation has been abated, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.19, Abatement verification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.notCovered: Dollar amounts of OSHA penalties (1903.15(d)). They are adjusted for inflation every year, so check the current eCFR text.

topics.name: Who must keep injury and illness records

points.text: Part 1904 requires employers to record and report work-related fatalities, injuries and illnesses. Recording or reporting a case does not mean anyone was at fault or that an OSHA rule was violated.
points.quote: Recording or reporting a work-related injury, illness, or fatality does not mean that the employer or employee was at fault, that an OSHA rule has been violated, or that the employee is eligible for workers' compensation or other benefits.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.0, Purpose (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: A company that had 10 or fewer employees at all times during the last calendar year does not need to keep OSHA injury and illness records unless OSHA or BLS informs it in writing that it must.
points.quote: If your company had 10 or fewer employees at all times during the last calendar year, you do not need to keep OSHA injury and illness records unless OSHA or the Bureau of Labor Statistics informs you in writing that you must keep records under § 1904.41 or § 1904.42.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.1, Partial exemption for employers with 10 or fewer employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Even partially exempt employers must report to OSHA any work-related incident resulting in a fatality, in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye.
points.quote: However, as required by § 1904.39, all employers covered by the OSH Act must report to OSHA any work-related incident that results in a fatality, the in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees, an employee amputation, or an employee loss of an eye.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.1, Partial exemption for employers with 10 or fewer employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Establishments in the industries listed in non-mandatory Appendix A to Subpart B (retail, information, finance, professional services, schools, health offices, restaurants and similar) are partially exempt unless asked in writing to keep records. No construction industry appears on that list.
points.quote: Employers are not required to keep OSHA injury and illness records for any establishment classified in the following North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes, unless they are asked in writing to do so by OSHA, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), or a state agency operating under the authority of OSHA or the BLS.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR Part 1904, Subpart B, Appendix A (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Employers record the cases of all employees on their payroll (labor, executive, hourly, salary, part-time, seasonal or migrant) and of employees not on their payroll whom they supervise on a day-to-day basis.
points.quote: You also must record the recordable injuries and illnesses that occur to employees who are not on your payroll if you supervise these employees on a day-to-day basis.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.31, Covered employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: If a contractor's employee is under the contractor's day-to-day supervision, the contractor records the case. If you supervise that worker day to day, you record it.
points.quote: If the contractor's employee is under the day-to-day supervision of the contractor, the contractor is responsible for recording the injury or illness.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.31, Covered employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: For activities where employees do not work at a single physical location, such as construction, the establishment is represented by the main or branch offices that supervise the activities or are the base for the workers.
points.quote: For activities where employees do not work at a single physical location, such as construction; transportation; communications, electric, gas and sanitary services; and similar operations, the establishment is represented by main or branch offices, terminals, stations, etc. that either supervise such activities or are the base from which personnel carry out these activities.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.46, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.notCovered: Electronic submission of injury and illness data to OSHA (1904.41) and Bureau of Labor Statistics survey requests (1904.42).

topics.name: Recording cases: criteria and forms

points.text: An employer that must keep records records each fatality, injury and illness that is work-related, is a new case, and meets one or more of the general recording criteria (or the specific-case rules in 1904.8 to 1904.12).
points.quote: must record each fatality, injury and illness that: (1) Is work-related; and (2) Is a new case; and

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.4, Recording criteria (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: An injury or illness is work-related if an event or exposure in the work environment caused or contributed to it or significantly aggravated a preexisting condition. Work-relatedness is presumed for events or exposures in the work environment unless a listed exception applies.
points.quote: Work-relatedness is presumed for injuries and illnesses resulting from events or exposures occurring in the work environment, unless an exception in § 1904.5(b)(2) specifically applies.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.5, Determination of work-relatedness (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: A case meets the general recording criteria if it results in death, days away from work, restricted work or transfer to another job, medical treatment beyond first aid, or loss of consciousness, or is a significant injury or illness diagnosed by a physician or other licensed health care professional.
points.quote: if it results in any of the following: death, days away from work, restricted work or transfer to another job, medical treatment beyond first aid, or loss of consciousness.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.7, General recording criteria (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: First aid, as defined in 1904.7, includes items such as cleaning, flushing or soaking surface wounds and using wound coverings like bandages; sutures and staples are medical treatment.
points.quote: Using wound coverings such as bandages, Band-AidsTM, gauze pads, etc.; or using butterfly bandages or Steri-StripsTM (other wound closing devices such as sutures, staples, etc., are considered medical treatment);

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.7, General recording criteria (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Employers use the OSHA 300 (Log of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses), 300-A (Summary) and 301 (Injury and Illness Incident Report) forms, or equivalent forms.
points.quote: The OSHA 300 form is called the Log of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses, the 300-A is the Summary of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses, and the OSHA 301 form is called the Injury and Illness Incident Report.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.29, Forms (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Each recordable case must be entered on the 300 Log and the 301 Incident Report within seven (7) calendar days of receiving information that it occurred.
points.quote: You must enter each recordable injury or illness on the OSHA 300 Log and 301 Incident Report within seven (7) calendar days of receiving information that a recordable injury or illness has occurred.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.29, Forms (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.notCovered: The detailed rules for counting days away and restricted work, determining new cases (1904.6), and specific cases such as needlesticks, medical removal, hearing loss and tuberculosis (1904.8 to 1904.11).

topics.name: Annual summary, retention and employee access

points.text: The annual summary (300-A) must be posted no later than February 1 of the following year and kept posted until April 30.
points.quote: You must post the summary no later than February 1 of the year following the year covered by the records and keep the posting in place until April 30.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.32, Annual summary (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The 300 Log, the privacy case list (if any), the annual summary and the 301 forms must be kept for five (5) years following the end of the calendar year they cover, and stored 300 Logs must be updated during that period.
points.quote: You must save the OSHA 300 Log, the privacy case list (if one exists), the annual summary, and the OSHA 301 Incident Report forms for five (5) years following the end of the calendar year that these records cover.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.33, Retention and updating (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Employers must set up a reasonable procedure for employees to report work-related injuries and illnesses promptly and accurately. A procedure is not reasonable if it would deter or discourage a reasonable employee from reporting.
points.quote: A procedure is not reasonable if it would deter or discourage a reasonable employee from accurately reporting a workplace injury or illness;

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.35, Employee involvement (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Employers must tell each employee that employees have the right to report work-related injuries and illnesses and that employers may not discharge or discriminate against them for reporting.
points.quote: Employers are prohibited from discharging or in any manner discriminating against employees for reporting work-related injuries or illnesses; and

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.35, Employee involvement (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: When an employee, former employee, personal representative or authorized employee representative asks for a copy of the 300 Log, it must be provided by the end of the next business day, free the first time.
points.quote: you must give the requester a copy of the relevant OSHA 300 Log(s) by the end of the next business day.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.35, Employee involvement (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: When an authorized government representative asks for the Part 1904 records, the employer must provide copies within four (4) business hours.
points.quote: When an authorized government representative asks for the records you keep under part 1904, you must provide copies of the records within four (4) business hours.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.40, Providing records to government representatives (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: A work-related fatality must be reported to OSHA within eight (8) hours after the death.
points.quote: Within eight (8) hours after the death of any employee as a result of a work-related incident, you must report the fatality to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: An in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees, an amputation, or a loss of an eye from a work-related incident must be reported within twenty-four (24) hours.
points.quote: Within twenty-four (24) hours after the in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees or an employee's amputation or an employee's loss of an eye, as a result of a work-related incident, you must report the in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye to OSHA.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Reports are made by telephone or in person to the nearest OSHA Area Office, by the toll-free number 1-800-321-OSHA (1-800-321-6742), or electronically on osha.gov. If the Area Office is closed, a message, fax or email is not enough.
points.quote: By telephone to the OSHA toll-free central telephone number, 1-800-321-OSHA (1-800-321-6742).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: A motor vehicle accident in a construction work zone must be reported. One on a public street or highway outside a construction work zone does not have to be reported, but must still be recorded if the employer keeps records.
points.quote: If the motor vehicle accident occurred in a construction work zone, you must report the fatality, in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: A fatality must be reported only if it occurs within thirty (30) days of the incident; an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye only if it occurs within twenty-four (24) hours of the incident.
points.quote: You must only report a fatality to OSHA if the fatality occurs within thirty (30) days of the work-related incident.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: In-patient hospitalization means a formal admission to the in-patient service of a hospital or clinic for care or treatment. Admission only for observation or diagnostic testing does not have to be reported.
points.quote: OSHA defines in-patient hospitalization as a formal admission to the in-patient service of a hospital or clinic for care or treatment.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)
